source_text: Ὃν τρόπον δὲ καὶ ἀνεθήκαμεν ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεῷ καινοποιηθέντες διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐξηγησόμεθα, ὅπως μὴ τοῦτο παραλιπόντες δόξωμεν πονηρεύειν τι ἐν τῇ ἐξηγήσει. Ὅσοι ἂν πεισθῶσι καὶ πιστεύωσιν ἀληθῆ ταῦτα τὰ ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν διδασκόμενα καὶ λεγόμενα εἶναι, καὶ βιοῦν οὕτως δύνασθαι ὑπισχνῶνται, εὔχεσθαί τε καὶ αἰτεῖν νηστεύοντες παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῶν προημαρτημένων ἄφεσιν διδάσκονται, ἡμῶν συνευχομένων καὶ συννηστευόντων αὐτοῖς. Ἔπειτα ἄγονται ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν, ἔνθα ὕδωρ ἐστί, καὶ τρόπον ἀναγεννήσεως, ὃν καὶ ἡμεῖς αὐτοὶ ἀνεγεννήθημεν, ἀναγεννῶνται· ἐπ᾿ ὀνόματος γὰρ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν ὅλων καὶ δεσπότου θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ πνεῦματος ἁγίου τὸ ἐν τῷ ὕδατι τότε λουτρὸν ποιοῦνται. Καὶ γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς εἶπεν· Ἂν μὴ ἀναγεννηθῆτε, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.“ Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ἀδύνατον εἰς τὰς μήτρας τῶν τεκουσῶν τοὺς ἅπαξ γεννωμένους ἐμβῆναι, φανερὸν πᾶσίν ἐστι. Καὶ διὰ Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου, ὡς προεγράψαμεν, εἴρηται, τίνα τρόπον φεύξονται τὰς ἁμαρτίας οἱ ἁμαρτήσαντες καὶ μετανοοῦντες. Ἐλέχθη δὲ οὕτως· Λούσασθε, καθαροὶ γένεσθε, ἀφέλετε τὰς πονηρίας ἀπὸ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν, μάθετε καλὸν ποιεῖν, κρίνατε ὀρφανῷ καὶ δικαιώσατε χήραν, καὶ δεῦτε καὶ διαλεχθῶμεν, λέγει κύριος· καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ὑμῶν ὡς φοινικοῦν, ὡσεὶ ἔριον λευκανῶ, καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν ὡς κόκκινον, ὡς χιόνα λευκανῶ. Ἐὰν δὲ μὴ εἰσακούσητέ μου, μάχαιρα ὑμᾶς κατέδεται· τὸ γὰρ στόμα κυρίου ἐλάλησε ταῦτα“. Καὶ λόγον δὲ εἰς τοῦτο παρὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐμάθομεν τοῦτον. Ἐπειδὴ τὴν πρώτην γένεσιν ἡμῶν ἀγνοοῦντες κατ᾿ ἀνάγκην γεγεννήμεθα ἐξ ὑγρᾶς σπορᾶς κατὰ μῖξιν τὴν τῶν γονέων πρὸς ἀλλήλους καὶ ἐν ἔθεσι φαύλοις καὶ πονηραῖς ἀναστροφαῖς γεγόναμεν, ὅπως μὴ ἀνάγκης τέκνα μηδὲ ἀγνοίας μένωμεν ἀλλὰ προαιρέσεως καὶ ἐπιστήμης, ἀφέσεώς ἁμαρτιῶν ὧν προημάρτομεν τύχωμεν, ἐν τῷ ὕδατι ἐπονομάζεται τῷ ἑλομένῳ ἀναγεννηθῆναι καὶ μετανοήσαντι ἐπὶ τοῖς ἡμαρτημένοις τὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν ὅλων καὶ δεσπότου θεοῦ ὄνομα, αὐτὸ τοῦτο μόνον ἐπιλέγοντος τοῦ τὸν λουσόμενον ἄγοντος ἐπὶ τὸ λουτρόν. Ὄνομα γὰρ τῷ ἀῤῥήτῳ θεῷ οὐδεὶς ἔχει εἰπεῖν· εἰ δέ τις τολμήσειεν εἶναι λέγειν, μέμηνε τὴν ἄσωτον μανίαν. Καλεῖται δὲ τοῦτο τὸ λουτρὸν φωτισμός, ὡς φωτιζομένων τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν ταῦτα μανθανόντων. Καὶ ἐπ᾿ ὀνόματος δὲ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ σταυρωθέντος ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, καὶ ἐπ᾿ ὀνόματος πνεύματος ἁγίου, ὃ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν προεκήρυξε τὰ κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν πάντα, ὁ φωτιζόμενος λούεται.
pass_a_gloss: But in what manner we have devoted ourselves to God, being renewed through Christ, we will explain, so that, having omitted this, we may not seem to be doing something evil in the explanation. Whoever will be persuaded and will believe that these things, which are taught and said by us, are true, and will promise to be able to live in this way, are taught, while fasting, to pray and to ask from God forgiveness for the things they have previously sinned, with us praying and fasting together with them. Then they are led by us to where there is water, and in the manner of rebirth, which also we ourselves were reborn, they are reborn; for in the name of the Father of all and the Master God and our Savior Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit, they then make the washing in the water. And Christ said: 'Unless you are reborn, you will not enter into the kingdom of heaven.' That it is also impossible for those who have been born once to enter into the wombs of those who gave birth to them is clear to all. And through Isaiah the prophet, as we have written before, it has been said, in what manner those who have sinned and are repenting will flee from sins. It has been said thus: 'Wash yourselves, become clean, remove the evil things from your souls, learn to do good, judge the orphan and justify the widow, and come and let us reason together,' says the Lord; 'and if your sins are like scarlet, I will whiten them like snow, and if they are like crimson, I will whiten them like wool.' But if you do not listen to me, a sword will devour you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things. And we have learned this word for this purpose from the apostles. Since, not knowing our first birth, we were necessarily born from moist seed according to the mixture of our parents with each other, and we became in foul and evil habits, so that we may not remain children of necessity or ignorance, but of choice and knowledge, and may obtain forgiveness of sins which we previously committed, in the water the name of the Father of all and the Master God is invoked upon the one who chooses to be reborn and has repented for the things they have sinned, the one who leads the one being washed to the washing invoking only this name. For no one has the name to say to the unutterable God; but if someone dares to say it, they have a reckless madness. This washing is called enlightenment, as the mind of those learning these things is enlightened. And upon the name of Jesus Christ, who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, and upon the name of the Holy Spirit, who proclaimed through the prophets all things concerning Jesus, the one being enlightened is washed.

choices.english: judge the orphan and justify the widow
rejected: seek justice, correct oppression; defend the orphan, plead for the widow

pass_b_english: I will explain how we devoted ourselves to God after being renewed through Christ, so that by covering this point we may not appear to be doing something wrong in our account. Those who are persuaded and believe that what we teach and say is true, and who promise they can live accordingly, are taught to pray and ask God for forgiveness of their past sins while fasting, with us praying and fasting alongside them. Then we lead them to where there is water, and they are reborn in the same manner of rebirth that we ourselves experienced. For in the name of God, the Father of all and our Master, and of our Savior Jesus Christ, and of the Holy Spirit, they undergo the washing in the water. Christ said, "Unless you are born again, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven" (John 3:5). It is obvious to everyone that those who have been born once cannot re-enter the wombs of those who gave birth to them. Through the prophet Isaiah, as we wrote earlier, it was declared how those who have sinned and repent will escape their sins. The words are: "Wash yourselves, become clean, remove the evil from your souls, learn to do good, seek justice for the orphan, defend the widow, and come now, let us reason together," says the Lord. "Though your sins are like scarlet, I will make them white as snow; though they are like crimson, I will make them white as wool. But if you refuse to listen, the sword will devour you, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken" (Isaiah 1:16–20). We learned this teaching from the apostles for this very reason. Since we were born by necessity from moist seed through the union of our parents, without knowledge of our first birth, and fell into foul and evil habits, we must not remain children of necessity and ignorance but become children of choice and knowledge, obtaining forgiveness for the sins we previously committed. Over the one who chooses to be reborn and has repented of their sins, the name of God, the Father of all and our Master, is invoked in the water as the one leading them to the washing pronounces that name alone. No one can utter a name for the unutterable God; anyone who dares claim to do so displays reckless madness. This washing is called enlightenment, because the minds of those learning these things are enlightened. And in the name of Jesus Christ, who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, and in the name of the Holy Spirit, who foretold through the prophets all things concerning Jesus, the one being enlightened is washed.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that correctly identifies the scripture citations (John 3:5 and Isaiah 1:16-20) which were alluded to in the Greek. The distinction between the 'first birth' (necessity) and 'rebirth' (choice) is preserved. The theological nuances regarding the invocation of the name and the unutterable nature of God are maintained.
